rows.evidence: Q1: Methods and Results sections <U+2013> the authors run their own HSPF watershed model simulations (calibrated/validated against 2014<U+2013>2015 observed streamflow and water quality, Table S5) driven by five bias-corrected GCM projections, and report their own tabulated and regressed results (Tables 1<U+2013>3, Figs. 3<U+2013>11).
rows.notes: The study does not involve remote sensing at all: soil moisture is an output of the HSPF model, not a satellite SSM retrieval, and there is no SSM-to-RZSM transformation. It also reports nothing on crop production or yield forecasting; the outcomes are runoff, ET, sediment, TN, TP and fecal coliform loads in a 3.27 km2 catchment upstream of the Miyun Reservoir under RCP 8.5. What the study actually shows is that modelled antecedent soil water content, antecedent drought days and precipitation amount jointly affect runoff and pollutant export, with heavy rain/rainstorms after prolonged drought producing the largest loads. Hence no own evidence on remote sensing delivering crop-yield information.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods and Results sections <U+2013> own HSPF model runs calibrated against observed 2014<U+2013>2015 data and forced with five GCMs; own results in Tables 1<U+2013>3 and Figs. 3<U+2013>11.
rows.notes: No remote-sensing product or SSM retrieval is used or evaluated; soil moisture values are HSPF model outputs. The study's 'climate-resilient management' content is limited to a general statement that findings can guide adaptive management of the drinking-water source and that BMP evaluation is future work; it does not test any management action or any remote-sensing-based risk-management tool. What it shows is modelled synergistic effects of drought duration and heavy rainfall on runoff, sediment, nutrient and fecal coliform loads, with antecedent soil water content as a key explanatory variable (Table 3). The study does state uncertainties/limitations of its own modelling (GCM, HSPF structure) and gives ranges across GCMs, but these do not relate to the claimed remote-sensing effect, so Q8/Q9 remain 'no' per the Q2 rule.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a watershed-scale HSPF modelling assessment of drought and rainfall-pattern impacts on hydrology and nonpoint source pollution under RCP 8.5; it has no remote-sensing, crop-yield, or irrigation-scheduling component, so both claim rows are a technology mismatch. The review appears to cite it loosely for the general relevance of soil moisture to climate-resilient management.
